correctness.rationale: Fourier orthogonality at n+1 equally spaced nodes produces the exact Poisson diagonal for all n and all nonnegative radii. Stirling yields the rate I(s|a)=a-s+s log(s/a). The two-interval covering proof identifies a unique touching configuration: first center a=R with rightmost endpoint eR, and second b solving I(1|b)=R; matching at s=eR gives rho-1=e log rho and (rho-1)R-1-log(rho R)=0. Strict convexity and monotonic endpoint motion rule out a smaller covering level and prove unique centers; extended-subsequence Poisson estimates pass this minimax optimum to arbitrary radius sequences. The standalone checker includes 19,561 finite assertions and direct complex matrix comparisons. No numerical calculation is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The object is a natural constrained Gaussian coherent-state sampling design for an (n+1)-dimensional Hermite/Fock band. The exact exponential lower-frame decay constant quantifies the best possible instability even with twice as many full angular samples as coefficients. The optimum improves the one-ring Poisson radius 1/e to 0.10557336..., and forces the two normalized radii to unique distinct limits. This gives a sharp obstruction and actionable radial allocation geometry; the result is not merely routine diagonalization.
